note: Our own list: firmwares the FM-1 Firmware Hub does not list (this repository's FM-1 SID, M-VAVE's own, and a few from fm1-editor.com/firmware). Edit this file to add one; node tools/hub_catalog.mjs appends these to the Hub's list in web/firmwares.json. An entry whose id the Hub lists too keeps its texts here and takes the Hub's package. "default": the firmware the page starts with.

firmwares.name: M-VAVE stock firmware
firmwares.author: M-VAVE
firmwares.about: The firmware the FM-1 ships with: a DX7-style FM synth, both cores running. This page does not host it and cannot download it (M-VAVE's server does not allow other pages to): download FM-1.fwsc from M-VAVE, then open it here; this browser keeps it for next time. Its patches live in flash an update does not carry, so it starts with a small bank of the emulator's own; "DX7 bank…" loads a 32-voice .syx.

firmwares.name: April OS
firmwares.author: beashoko
firmwares.license: MIT (its repository, which holds the installer page; the firmware source is not published)
firmwares.about: A sampler inspired by the Casio SK-1: no synth engines, only samples, recorded through the installer page's microphone bridge.

firmwares.name: fm1-dock
firmwares.author: joakimeriksson
firmwares.about: One firmware, many synths: CS-1, Scintilla and OberVave as modules in flash, the sine built in; HOME opens the picker. Add FM-106, MONK-1, FiMba-1, GATOR, DUB-1, FM-1 SID, AMB-1 or FoMni from its page with one click; Bluetooth MIDI with both cores, a master EQ, MIDI options. Formerly harbor.

firmwares.name: FM-1 Doom
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.about: Doom on the FM-1: one arena from FreeDM, played on the keys and a knob, on the FM-1's screen, with synthesised sound effects and no music.

firmwares.name: FM1 Quest
firmwares.author: hericdk
firmwares.about: A live RPG adventure inside the synth.

firmwares.name: FM-1 SID
firmwares.author: joakimeriksson
firmwares.about: A SID chip on the FM-1, its own firmware on fm1-dock (fm1-dock's USB, installer and rescue; the sine as the fallback): a C64 tune player (reSID 0.16 and a 6510 running the tune's own code, PSID and RSID) starting with GoatTracker 2's example songs, Dojo first; a GoatTracker editor; and a synth: the keys play 12 instruments, KNOB1-4 are cutoff, resonance, attack, release; FX opens chorus, delay and reverb. Its page plays all of HVSC and sends any .sid to a real FM-1 over USB (Play on my FM-1), and the FM-1's keys play the page. Installed and playing on a real FM-1: joakimeriksson.github.io/fm1-emu/fm1-sid/

firmwares.name: SLOOP ALG
firmwares.author: shaw-core
firmwares.about: A SLOOP test build with extra FM algorithms.
